actions.action: Unroll a new leaf or check stem tips with a magnifier or phone camera for thrips
Place blue or yellow sticky traps near the plant and monitor counts
Check philodendrons and syngoniums for thrips
Remove the most damaged leaves and heavily scarred new growth
Spray spinosad on leaf tops, undersides and stems and drench soil surface every 5-7 days for 3-4 weeks
Scrape off the top inch or two of soil and replace with fresh mix
Isolate the plant away from other plants
Check leaf undersides for spider mite webbing or speckles
Flush the soil to clear mineral buildup

reason: Thrips is correctly named as the main cause, but the answer relies on repeated spinosad sprays and soil top-dressing rather than the systemic granules that cleared the infestation, so the advice only partly matches; nothing it recommends is harmful.
